property_summary: For any input where all internal calls succeed, the transfer function must return true; the mutant breaks this by returning false even when all inner transfers succeed.

For any input where all internal calls succeed and complete without revert, the return value of P.transfer matches the success of its execution (always true when no revert), whereas M.transfer returns false for the same non-reverting calls.

If the transfer function succeeds without reverting, then for every recipient address, an external call must have been attempted (and succeeded), which implies the function must have iterated over the array and made calls.
If the function does not revert, then the external contract must have been called exactly _tos.length times.
If transfer returns true, then either _tos.length is 0 (impossible by require) or at least one external call to the token contract must have succeeded.
If transfer does not revert, then for at least one address in _tos, no subsequent transfer with the same caddress should succeed unless the token allowance has been restored.
If transfer does not revert, then at least one external call was attempted, so the total number of external calls made by c across all transactions must be greater than zero.

The reference contract always either returns true or reverts from an internal require, while the mutant always reverts due to the inserted revert() at the start, causing any successful return to differ.
A call to transfer must not revert if all internal calls succeed, but the mutant reverts unconditionally.
For any input, a call to transfer must either revert or return true; the mutant always reverts due to the inserted revert(), violating the possibility of returning true.
A call to transfer must not revert when _tos is non-empty and the caddress sub-calls succeed, but the mutant reverts unconditionally due to the inserted revert() at the start of the function body.

For any admissible input where _tos is non-empty and the sub-calls succeed, a call to transfer must return true; the mutant always reverts due to the upfront revert(), so it cannot return true for any such input.
